ablation_cumulative_orbit_counts.verdict: R13 = R14 = R12 at every k: both new filters are INERT at Level 0.
ablation_cumulative_orbit_counts.proof: A Level-0 orbit dies only if EVERY decoration of it dies.  The all-corner decoration (every square-square contact a corner type, every wall contact a wall-corner) always exists -- its tilt system is a strict digraph on k singleton classes with no zero pin, and every graph has at least one acyclic orientation.  It carries NO flush component, so RULER is vacuous on it; and its charge is 0 under min-over-bins semantics (every non-flush square-square contact can be realized as CC, which is uncharged by design).  Even pricing every one of its wall-corner contacts at the ownership ceiling 1/16 gives at most 12/16 = 0.75 (per-wall <= 3 caps the wall incidences at 12) against B0 = 4.0318.  So no Level-0 orbit can be killed by either filter, at any k.

sample_check.statement: On every sampled (graph, wall-mask) pair, surviving decoration weight we_surv - ruler_kill - charge_kill is strictly positive.

split_by_theorem_A45_2.b_killable: ALL of it, for k >= 10, EXACTLY.  In a MAIN structure every square-square component carries at least one wall contact (L3, no floating component -- components merge only through shared wall bits, so a wall-less component has mask 0 and is rejected).  In a ZERO-CHARGE decoration every wall contact is WF, so every component is zero-pinned and ALL k loaded squares sit at tilt class 0.  A26 caps the number of squares within 2.503 deg of class 0 at 9.  Hence every zero-charge core with k >= 10 is DEAD -- and this needs no k=11 join, because the cap is a universal statement about the packing, not an existential one.  Measured premise: zero_charge_every_component_walled = True on every sampled structure at every k.
split_by_theorem_A45_2.c_killable: the RULER/Lemma-Q column measured WITHIN the zero-charge class: {3: 0.6, 4: 0.6643, 5: 0.7763, 6: 0.7676, 7: 0.6128} of zero-charge decoration weight per k.  Mechanism: a flush component that carries WF anchors on OPPOSITE walls at FL-graph distance <= 2 cannot span s - 1 in [2.80, 2.877084] (each link moves that projection by at most 1).  This is the only mechanism that bites at k <= 9.
split_by_theorem_A45_2.e_residue: EMPTY inside this census.  Residue (e) is the floating flush component with a free common tilt; MAIN's L3 filter already forbids components with no wall contact, so no surviving structure has one.  (e) therefore contributes 0 here and reappears only if L3 is dropped.
split_by_theorem_A45_2.f_residue: THE WHOLE RESIDUE.  For k <= 9 a zero-charge core is consistent with A26: 9 or fewer class-0 squares plus 11-k rattlers of any tilt.  Nothing in the calculus touches it.  Share of decorations: {3: '3.82e-02', 4: '5.72e-03', 5: '6.44e-04', 6: '6.22e-05', 7: '5.12e-06'}, falling roughly geometrically in k.

m_ub_table.method: A45-B  m_ub(theta) crude guard  [EXACT, cheap]  --  notes/charging_lemma.md Sec 6.4.
m_ub_table.deviation: the brief calls the eroded region an octagon; the Minkowski erosion of a square by a square is a SQUARE (4 edges), and the count below is done on that exact rotated-square region.
m_ub_table.verdict: the crude tier delivers m_ub <= 10 on exactly ONE bin, [0,3) -> 9 (which A26 already had, out to 2.503 deg).  From 3 deg up the bound is 12 (bins up to 18 deg) or 14, so GAP-A45-Z1 stands on 14 of 15 bins.  Mechanism: the eroded region's bounding box in the theta-frame has side w(s0-w) with w = cos+sin, which crosses 3 at about 4 deg and forces a 4th column of centres.

charge_ceiling.statement: TABLE-INDEPENDENT: charge(K) <= area B(p, rho_min/2) = rho_min^2 (Sec 4 definition (ii): the certified region list lives inside the half-moat box), and rho_min <= 1/4 (top of the Sec 5 moat ladder).  A candidate structure has E <= 3k+2 contacts (A31 L4(a), a HARD filter of MAIN).  So the total charge of ANY k <= 11 structure is at most (3k+2)/16.

pilot_calibration.note: the pilot ships WC at rho = 3/16 and CE at rho = 1/16 and DROPS CC (no moat), so rho_min <= 1/16 and every charged region lives in a box of area <= 1/256 = 0.00390625.

charge_ceiling.verdict: at k = 11 the ceiling is 35/16 = 2.1875 against B0 = 4.031780343056 -- short by a factor 1.843.  Theorem A45.1 CANNOT fire on an 11-square structure with the half-moat ownership scheme, whatever the certified table says.  To fire it would need a mean charge of 0.1152 per contact, i.e. rho_min >= 0.3394, which is off the top of the moat ladder (0.25).  The weighted-Voronoi refinement of Sec 4 remark 2 buys radius (rho_i+rho_j)/4 <= 1/8, the same order, so it does not change the verdict.

mechanisms.M1_LemmaQ_path_bound: opposite-wall WF anchors at FL-graph distance <= 2: the projection must equal s-1 in [2.80, 2.877084] and a path of m links moves it by at most m
mechanisms.M2_odd_cycle_parity: a same-wall pin set equalises one family across the component, forcing every FL link into the OTHER family; an odd cycle of +-1 steps cannot close
mechanisms.M3_LemmaQ_integrality: let P = the component squares pinned in one family to the SAME wall kind; every FL link inside P is forced into the OTHER family, so that family's differences inside P are INTEGERS; if P also carries a LO and a HI anchor of that family joined inside P, the difference must be an integer equal to s-1 in [2.80, 2.877084], which contains no integer -- Lemma Q verbatim.

ruler_kill_audit.verdict: every RULER kill is a WALL-ANCHORED flush component -- 411 of 411 killed component signatures at k = 3..5 are zero-pinned -- and all of them fall into three named mechanisms with NOTHING left over.  Lemma R's pure length cap contributes ZERO kills, because a decoration never forces the normal family or the sign, so a ruler is never forced to be long.

CHARGE: 2 to 4 corner contacts need 1.008-2.016 of charge each to reach B0, against an ownership ceiling of 0.0625.  Both inert by 16x-32x.

gaps.text: CHARGE cannot fire at k <= 11.  Table-independent: the half-moat ownership box caps a contact at rho_min^2 <= 1/16 and Euler caps the contact count at 3k+2, so the maximum conceivable sum at k=11 is 2.1875 < B0 = 4.0318.  With the CERTIFIED table actually shipped (rho_min = 1/16, max entry 6.256e-04) the same maximum is 0.0219, short by 184x.  Closing that gap needs a mean charge of 0.1152 per contact, i.e. rho_min >= 0.3394, which is off the top of the moat ladder and far above every radius the pilot could certify.

Even below the ceiling, the census-side semantics zero almost everything: a non-flush square-square contact of a DECORATION can always be realized as CC (uncharged by design), a wall-degree-2 square can realize the WCC container-corner case (uncharged, lead addendum), and a class tilt window that spans a dropped bin contributes 0.  To price a contact at all, the enumeration would have to resolve CE-vs-CC per edge AND carry a tilt window narrow enough to exclude every dropped bin -- neither of which an H1 decoration carries.  This is the A43 enumeration-certificate mismatch again, now on the family that was supposed to evade it.

The CSP relaxes slides to [-1,1], imposes no interior-disjointness inside a flush component, and gives non-zero-pinned components the widest tilt window (cos+sin <= sqrt2).  Components with more than 12 FL links fall back to the path relaxation (a sub-system, so kills stay sound) and to an unrefined 4^m gauge count.  Every one of these can only ADD survivors.

All Level-1 numbers use A43's sampling protocol (seed 7, cap 160 graphs, 40 at k=7, edge budget 22), so they are weighted sample means, not exhaustive.  k = 8..11 are 3-model fits with a k=7 holdout, not bounds -- same status as A31/A43.

The m_ub table is a cover bound (columns of width < 1, each holding at most 1 + floor(y-extent) centres), computed per 3-deg bin with interval arithmetic and sub-binning.  It is not sharp: a B&B in the style of A08 would lower it.  As it stands GAP-A45-Z1 (single-grain mid-tilt residue) is open on 14 of 15 bins.
All A43-G2..G7 and A31-G1..G7 gaps are inherited unchanged; the lambda0 = 0 branch is uncovered; rattler-join semantics (residue (f)) is the reason the zero-charge collapse only bites at k >= 10.

findings: RULER IS THE ONLY THING THAT BITES, AND IT BITES EXACTLY WHERE A43'S LAW SAYS.  As a decoration KILL it removes {3: '0.0107', 4: '0.0070', 5: '0.0057', 6: '0.0042', 7: '0.0023'} of decoration weight at k = 3..7 -- one part in a hundred or less.  The kill audit is unambiguous: 411 of 411 killed component signatures are ZERO-PINNED (wall-anchored), and they split into exactly three mechanisms with nothing left over -- M1 the Lemma-Q path bound (392: opposite-wall WF anchors at FL-graph distance <= 2, where the projection must equal s-1 in [2.80, 2.877084] but a path of m links moves it by at most m); M2 odd-cycle parity (16: a same-wall pin set equalises one family across the component, forcing every link into the other family, and an odd cycle of +-1 steps cannot close); M3 Lemma Q verbatim (3: the same forcing plus an opposite anchor pair makes the difference an INTEGER, and [2.80, 2.877084] contains no integer).  Lemma R's pure LENGTH cap contributes ZERO kills: a decoration never forces the normal family or the sign, so no ruler is ever forced to be long.  Bite proportional to pinned coordinates, one level below where A43 measured it.

THE REFINED FORM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE KILL FORM.  A31 prices a flush contact with a gauge multiplicity of 4 -- which is exactly the CSP's (normal family, sign) pair.  Counting only the FEASIBLE assignments instead of all 4 is still one-sided and still EXACT, and it keeps {3: '0.9480', 4: '0.9420', 5: '0.9394', 6: '0.9378', 7: '0.9275'} of the decoration count at k = 3..7.  On Trump's own structure the refinement is dramatic (1632 of 65536 assignments survive, the realized one among them) because his flush skeleton is heavily wall-anchored.

BOTH FILTERS ARE PROVABLY INERT AT LEVEL 0.  A Level-0 orbit dies only if every decoration dies, and the all-corner decoration always exists, has no flush component at all, and carries charge 0 under min-over-bins semantics.  R13 = R14 = R12 at every k -- the ablation table does not move.  The place the calculus can move a number is the decoration fan-out, i.e. the multiplier, not the orbit count.

THE CERTIFIED TABLE LANDED AND CONFIRMS IT WITH ROOM TO SPARE.  Agent A's results/charge_table.json ships rho_min = 1/16 (half-moat radius R = 1/32), 25 of 75 bins kept and 50 dropped for want of a moat, every kept entry exact-recertified.  Its LARGEST entry is 41/65536 = 6.256e-04.  Even charging all 35 Euler-maximal contacts of a k=11 structure at that maximum gives 0.0219 against B0 = 4.0318 -- short by a factor of 184.  And the census-side min-over-window is exactly 0 in any case: WC bins 0-2 (phi < 9 deg) are dropped, and every CE mismatch bin has a dropped u-sub-bin, so an unrestricted class window always reaches a zero.

CHARGE IS INERT BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS TABLE-INDEPENDENT.  Ownership caps a contact at the area of its half-moat box, rho_min^2 <= (1/4)^2 = 1/16; Euler caps the contact count at 3k+2 = 35 at k = 11; so the largest charge sum any 11-square structure can carry is 2.1875 against a budget of 4.031780343056.  Short by 1.84x at the theoretical maximum.  Calibrated on agent A's pilot -- WC shipped at rho = 3/16, CE at rho = 1/16, CC DROPPED -- the global rho_min is at most 1/16, the half-moat box has area at most 1/256, and the k=11 ceiling falls to 0.1367: short by 29.5x.  Firing the filter would need rho_min >= 0.3394, off the top of the shipped ladder.  The census-side min-over-realizations semantics then zeroes what little is left (CC reachable from every non-flush contact; WCC for wall-degree-2 squares; dropped bins).

ZERO-CHARGE COLLAPSE: (b) TAKES ALL OF IT AT k >= 10, EXACTLY, AND NOTHING BELOW.  In MAIN every component has a wall contact (L3), so a zero-charge decoration pins every component to class 0 and puts all k loaded squares at tilt 0; A26 allows at most 9 such squares.  So zero-charge cores with k >= 10 are dead outright -- no k=11 join needed, since A26's cap is universal, not existential.  Below k = 10 the residue is entirely (f), the rattler caveat, and residue (e) (floating common-tilt components) is EMPTY because L3 already forbids them.  The zero-charge share of decorations is small and falling: {3: '3.82e-02', 4: '5.72e-03', 5: '6.44e-04', 6: '6.22e-05', 7: '5.12e-06'}.  Within it, RULER/Lemma Q kills {3: '0.60', 4: '0.66', 5: '0.78', 6: '0.77', 7: '0.61'}.

m_ub(theta) CRUDE TIER: 9 on [0,3), 12 on [3,18), 14 on [18,45).  Exactly one bin delivers the m_ub <= 10 that the single-grain residue needs, and A26 already had that bin (out to 2.503 deg).  GAP-A45-Z1 stands on 14 of 15 bins.  The mechanism is crisp: the centre region's bounding box in the theta-frame has side w*(s0-w), w = cos+sin, which passes 3 at about 4 degrees and buys a fourth column of centres.

CANARIES ALL PASS (PASS).  Trump survives RULER with his realized (family,sign) assignment feasible in every component; his 5-square flush strip at 40.1819 deg has Lemma-R capacity 5.463650, margin 0.463650 (the brief's 0.4636); his 6 upright squares carry 9 WF and 3 FL contacts and zero wall-corner contacts, all charged exactly 0; and his total charge sum is under B0 with capture 1.65% of the budget at the realized bins of the stub table.

SPOT MEASUREMENT ON THE A43-H2 k=3 SPINE SURVIVORS: 0/10 kills from either filter, and RULER does not even trim a gauge assignment (all 10 survivors have C-C ends, hence no WF anchor, hence no pin).  The certified [18,72] / [12,78] windows do not help: the extent cap must use the LARGEST cos+sin in the window, and every one of these windows contains 45 degrees.

BOTTOM LINE.  I-L13's promise was a certificate whose unit of account matches the enumerated object.  It does match -- and it is still too small to pay.  The charging lemma is sound and its ownership scheme is honest, but the ownership box is two orders of magnitude smaller than the budget it has to exceed, so the arithmetic never closes.  The flush-ruler laws are the real find of this brief: they are EXACT, they bite on the gauge multiplicity rather than the orbit count, and they bite wherever a wall pins a coordinate -- the same law A43 measured, holding at a third level.
